statement: Let M = n*(n-1)/2. Let d_1 <= d_2 <= ... <= d_M be the nondecreasing list of the M values |nums[i] - nums[j]| obtained from all index pairs with 0 <= i < j < n, with one entry per pair, so equal distances are repeated. The function returns a result r and r = d_k (1-indexed).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^4; for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6; and 1 <= k <= n*(n-1)/2, where k is the integer value of the i64 parameter.

statement: For every nums and k satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; in particular, it does not fail because of overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^4; for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6; and 1 <= k <= n*(n-1)/2, where k is the integer value of the i64 parameter.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= max(nums) - min(nums), where max(nums) and min(nums) are the maximum and minimum values among nums[0],...,nums[n-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^4; for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6; and 1 <= k <= n*(n-1)/2, where k is the integer value of the i64 parameter.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist indices i and j with 0 <= i < j < n such that r = |nums[i] - nums[j]|.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^4; for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6; and 1 <= k <= n*(n-1)/2, where k is the integer value of the i64 parameter.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the number of index pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < j < n and |nums[i] - nums[j]| <= r is at least k.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^4; for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6; and 1 <= k <= n*(n-1)/2, where k is the integer value of the i64 parameter.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the number of index pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < j < n and |nums[i] - nums[j]| < r is less than k; equivalently, it is at most k-1. With repeated distances this number need not equal k-1; the valid rank characterization is count(<r) < k <= count(<=r).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^4; for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6; and 1 <= k <= n*(n-1)/2, where k is the integer value of the i64 parameter.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = min { |nums[i] - nums[j]| : 0 <= i < j < n }.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^4; for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6; and k = 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = max(nums) - min(nums).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^4; for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6; and k = n*(n-1)/2.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^4; for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6; and 1 <= k <= n*(n-1)/2. Let z be the number of index pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < j < n and nums[i] = nums[j]; assume k <= z.

statement: If the call smallest_distance_pair(nums, k) returns r and the call smallest_distance_pair(nums', k) returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^4; for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6; and 1 <= k <= n*(n-1)/2. Let nums' be any slice of i64 with len(nums') = n whose entries have the same multiset of values as nums, i.e. nums' is a permutation of nums.

statement: If the call smallest_distance_pair(nums, k1) returns r1 and the call smallest_distance_pair(nums, k2) returns r2, then r1 <= r2.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^4; for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6. Let k1 and k2 be integers with 1 <= k1 <= k2 <= n*(n-1)/2.

statement: If the call smallest_distance_pair(nums, k) returns r and the call smallest_distance_pair(nums_c, k) returns r_c, then r = r_c.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^4; for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6; and 1 <= k <= n*(n-1)/2. Let c be an integer such that 0 <= nums[i] + c <= 10^6 for every i. Define nums_c by nums_c[i] = nums[i] + c.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer x such that the number of index pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < j < n and |nums[i] - nums[j]| <= x is at least k, we have r <= x.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^4; for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6; and 1 <= k <= n*(n-1)/2, where k is the integer value of the i64 parameter.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is the least integer x such that the number of index pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < j < n and |nums[i] - nums[j]| <= x is at least k; equivalently, r = min { x in Z : #{ (i,j) : 0 <= i < j < n and |nums[i]-nums[j]| <= x } >= k }.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^4; for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6; and 1 <= k <= n*(n-1)/2, where k is the integer value of the i64 parameter.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if z >= k.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^4; for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6; and 1 <= k <= n*(n-1)/2. Let z be the number of index pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < j < n and nums[i] = nums[j].
